form.what: a multiplier on the candidate's residual spread, one per pressure-day type of the TARGET day, fitted at each refit and applied at every lead h = 1..5 of the forecasts that refit serves. The candidate's quantiles are centre + scale * (shift + pool_j), with pool_j the 23 empirical quantiles of the standardised residuals z of the refit's direct training pairs. An arm replaces pool_j by c + m * (pool_j - c), with c the pool's median (the grid level 0.5) and m the multiplier of the target day's type. The shift (the calendar and settlement terms), the centre, the scale at the anchor and the Huber fit are the candidate's, unchanged; m = 1 reproduces the candidate exactly. The SRF cap is applied after the multiplier, exactly as to the candidate (repo_model.s3c_candidate, margin 0 bp).
form.module: repo_model.day_type_scale (multipliers, rescaled_pool, DayTypeScale); the walk is spread_mr_state_calendar.walk with training_pairs = direct, unchanged, and the arms are made from its estimates after the walk (they add no fit, only the ratio below)
form.type_of_a_day: repo_model.turn_days.reporting_day_type, the record in force (#1135), on the day's own calendar columns: a function of the date alone, known years ahead, read at the target day for a training row and for a forecast
form.statistic: m_T = sqrt( mean over the refit's training pairs whose target day is of type T of (z - c)^2 / mean over all the refit's training pairs of (z - c)^2 ), z the pair's standardised residual after the terms (StateEstimate.residuals), computed per lead. The ratio is of root mean squares about the pool's median, so a type whose residuals are as spread as the whole pool has m = 1, and a type whose residuals are twice as spread has m = 2.
form.minimum_rows_rule: a type with fewer than 10 training pairs at a lead (target days of that type in the trailing window up to the anchor) has m = 1 at that lead; so has a refit where the all-pairs mean square is zero
form.bounds_rule: m is clamped to [0.5, 4.0]; the share of (refit, lead, type) cells at a bound or at the fallback is reported
form.training_rows: exactly the refit's direct training pairs: targets in the trailing window and at or before the anchor (spread_mean_reversion.training_rows), each required public by pb._require_public. A target after the anchor raises LookAheadError in repo_model.day_type_scale.multipliers

reading.which_reading: BY TYPE, declared before any score. The typed arm is read type by type on the pressure-day type of the target day (turn, quarter_end_turn, tax_date, year_end, ordinary), each with 20 or more target days, on grid CRPS and the 90% band coverage, against the candidate. The pooled-scale arm is read on the two groups it changes or leaves alone: all non-ordinary target days together (a gain there is its claim) and ordinary target days (which it leaves element for element as the candidate, so a difference there is a bug). A pooled figure over all days is shown but never read alone: a gain is a gain only where its type-level reading agrees, and a pooled gain that no type carries is not one. A type of fewer than 20 target days is listed with its coverage and not read
reading.primary: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5, paired with (s3c-ann-net), studentized stationary bootstrap, mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1402, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound), read from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009), with the skill interval beside it
reading.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
reading.benchmark: B1'* beside: both arms and the candidate against B1'* on the same three scores, pooled and by lead, regime and pressure-day type; the benchmark is not a threshold of this study
reading.splits: pooled; by lead; by regime (the declared regimes, 2018-19 and 2020 on their own among them); by pressure-day type of the target day (turn_days.reporting_day_type) and the union of the non-ordinary types; the 2026 days are the second window and carry the same splits. The intervals of a group of days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide
reading.coverage: the empirical coverage of the central 50% and 90% bands of the candidate and both arms, by regime, by pressure-day type and by the calendar target-day types of #1363 (candidate_calibration_1363.group_report: the stationary-bootstrap interval of a rate, groups of 20 or more target days read), and the serial dependence of the band-miss sequences by the reading in force at the base of this pull request: #1363's Christoffersen independence test with its permutation p-value and the protocol's thinned reading (scoring_protocol.coverage_cells). The thinned reading for leads 2 to 5 that #1400 declares is not on main and is not used; the page says so
reading.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested; a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1402, two-sided 90% interval; the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c-ann-net) stays the frozen H5 candidate.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and pressure-day-type splits beside it, and a gain is read by type (see reading.which_reading).

Nothing is adopted. Whether a day-type scale joins the registered candidate, and whether its result changes what the registration says about the known limits, is hers; the page ends with a marked question whose default changes no claim.
